_readme: The app's changelog, as the repository states it. This file is the source
of truth for everything the Updates side of the in-app bell shows.
WHAT GOES IN HERE
A change a household would actually notice. This is a changelog, not a
commit log — it is read by the people living in the house, and the bar is
"would somebody notice this without being told, and be glad they were?"
Yes: a new screen or capability; a change to how something already works
that people have to relearn; a fix for something people knew was broken;
anything that changes what the app costs, asks for or keeps.
No: refactors, renames, tests, dependency bumps, schema and index work, a
padding tweak, a colour, a performance win nobody could feel, a bug fixed
before anybody hit it. Not secrets — just not news. A changelog padded
with them is one people stop opening, which costs the entries that mattered.
One entry per release, not per commit. Six bullets under one headline beat
six headlines; that is what `highlights` is for. Write it for the
household, never for the repository.
Edit it in the SAME COMMIT as the work it describes, then:
cd backend && npx convex run inbox:syncChangelog "$(cat changelog.json)"
Idempotent by `slug`, so running it on every deploy is the intent. An entry
already published keeps its publication date — fixing a typo in an old note
does not move it to the top of everybody's feed or light the badge again.
FIELDS
slug       required, stable, unique. Convention: "<version>-<short-name>".
Changing it files a second entry; never change one after it
has shipped.
version    the app version this ships in. THIS IS A GATE, not a label:
a client on 1.8.1 draws a 1.9.0 entry as "coming soon" rather
than promising a button it does not have. Omit for an
announcement that is true on every build.
kind       feature | improvement | fix | announcement
title      one line, sentence case, no trailing full stop.
body       a short paragraph. What changed and why it is better.
highlights optional bullets. Up to 12, each one short enough to read at a
glance.
pinned     optional. Floats to the top until unpinned.
draft      optional. true keeps it out of the feed entirely.
Newest entries go at the TOP of `entries` — the file reads like the feed.

entries.title: Notifications and updates, in one place
entries.body: Every notification your household has ever sent now stays put. Tap the bell on the Home tab to scroll back through what everyone has been doing, filter it by what you care about, and read what has changed in the app itself — two feeds, one button.
highlights: Nothing is lost to a swiped-away banner any more
Filter the household feed by chores, money, shopping and the rest
A separate changelog, so app news never buries a leaking tap
Your own actions never light the badge
